samples.summary: New `lineAffinity` parameter on `findVisualLine` defaults to `'forward'`, which contradicts the repo-wide convention that line affinity defaults to `'backward'` (`cursor.ts:13`, `pagination.ts:385`, and `docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:381` — "Default `lineAffinity` is `'backward'`"). Choosing a back-compat default that differs from every other affinity default in the docs package means the same helper resolves a wrap boundary differently depending on which code path reaches it, and readers of the design docs will expect the other behavior. Preserving old behavior at the one un-updated call site could instead be expressed explicitly at that site.

The fix is threaded through `getVisualLineRange`/`Start`/`End` but the other in-package consumer of `findVisualLine` — the vertical-move "already on first/last visual line" check in `moveVertical` — is left on the (now explicit) `'forward'` default, so a caret sitting at a wrap boundary with `'backward'` affinity is still classified onto the following visual line there. If the issue's outcome is "visual-line resolution respects the caret's affinity" rather than specifically Home/End/Cmd+Backspace, this call site is an unfixed instance of the same defect; if the issue is narrowly scoped, this is just an inconsistency worth a comment.
samples.evidence: const info = findVisualLine(lb, pos); // no affinity passed, gets 'forward'

samples.summary: The three new optional `lineAffinity` parameters on `getVisualLineRange`, `getVisualLineStart` and `getVisualLineEnd` are never supplied by any caller (all three call sites — text-editor.ts:2786, 2799, 2845 — pass only `this.cursor.position` and rely on the default). Since the default already reads `this.cursor.lineAffinity`, the parameters are unexercised API surface on private methods; a plain read of `this.cursor.lineAffinity` inside `getVisualLineRange` would satisfy the issue with less surface. It also creates a latent trap: the parameter's default silently applies the *cursor's* affinity to whatever `pos` is handed in, which is only correct because every caller happens to pass the cursor position (as the docstring notes).
samples.evidence: getVisualLineRange(pos, lineAffinity = this.cursor.lineAffinity) — callers at 2786/2799/2845 pass one argument

samples.summary: Reuse: the cell-block branch of `getVisualLineRange` open-codes a third copy of the wrap-boundary rule that `findVisualLine` already implements (the diff's own comment says "Same boundary rule as findVisualLine"), and a fourth variant of the same rule lives in `moveCellLine` (text-editor.ts:3116-3122). The change propagates the duplication instead of extracting the boundary predicate (or a table-cell-line variant of `findVisualLine`) into `visual-line.ts`, so the next affinity fix has to be made in three places again.
samples.evidence: const ownsLineEnd = li === endLine - 1 || lineAffinity === 'backward'; // duplicate of visual-line.ts:38
